rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado business leaders grow more pessimistic about the local economy
rows.standfirst: Plus: As 84% of workers surveyed say they plan to keep working past retirement age, Colorado considers the benefits of an older workforce.

rows.title: One Navajo community finally gets electricity after more than 10 years. It’s still waiting for water.
rows.standfirst: Westwater, a small subdivision in Utah, has run into barrier after barrier for more than 20 years as it tries to bring clean, running water to its residents.

rows.title: Xcel Energy’s ability to meet next summer’s electricity demand hangs on two Pueblo solar projects
rows.standfirst: The transition from fossil-fuel generated electricity to renewables is proving tricky for Colorado’s largest utility.

rows.title: A Crested Butte couple just wanted better backpacking coffee. They made something so good NASA came calling.
rows.standfirst: Mark and Alison Drucker co-founded First Ascent in 2014 and brewed up instant coffee four years later. Their product is now headed to the International Space Station at the request of an astronaut.

rows.title: Vail Resorts rejects Town of Vail’s $12 million offer for parcel to protect bighorn, pushing council to create donor fund to fuel fight
rows.standfirst: Vail Resorts wants to build housing on the parcel. Town wants to protect the local bighorn herd. A prolonged legal battle now looms as the only resolution.

rows.title: Proposition 123: Should Colorado set aside nearly $300 million each year for affordable housing?
rows.standfirst: Proponents of the measure say it would help the state tackle one of its biggest problems, but naysayers worry about how it would affect the state budget and TABOR refunds

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado workers push back against the retirement age
rows.standfirst: Resources for older workers and employers who want to hire them. Plus: Companies announce HQ moves to the Denver area, new job openings and more.

rows.title: As places like Cañon City court redevelopment, they find an unlikely ally in the EPA
rows.standfirst: The agency’s brownfields program just came into lots of new money. And they want rural and small-town Colorado to help spend it.

rows.title: Amendment E: Colorado’s homestead property tax exemption would be extended to Gold Star spouses
rows.standfirst: Colorado voters will see Amendment E on their ballots this 2022 election. Here’s what it would do, plus the arguments for and against.

rows.title: New survey shows veteran homelessness has decreased 31% in metro Denver
rows.standfirst: The point-in-time count is a snapshot of homelessness on a given night. It helps human service leaders capture the overall size and demographics of the homeless population nationwide.

rows.title: Citizen scientists want clarity on hidden emissions from Pueblo’s coal-fired power plant
rows.standfirst: People in Pueblo are at the forefront of an emerging partnership between activists, conservationists and a newly created state unit to quantify environmental justice hotspots in Colorado communities and the toxic pollutants that bedevil them.

rows.title: Proposition 124: Colorado voters will decide whether retail liquor stores should be able to open more locations
rows.standfirst: The measure, backed by Total Wine & More and the national chain’s wealthy owners, would let liquor retailers open an unlimited number of stores in Colorado starting in 2037

rows.title: Proposition 125: Coloradans will decide whether grocery stores should be allowed to sell wine starting next year
rows.standfirst: Proposition 125 comes from a citizen initiative that is supported by major grocery stores.

rows.title: Proposition 126: Should Colorado restaurants be allowed to sell to-go cocktails forever?
rows.standfirst: Proposition 126 also would let third-party delivery services, like Uber Eats and DoorDash, deliver alcohol

rows.title: Joe Biden has made Colorado’s Camp Hale a national monument. Could a future president unravel it?
rows.standfirst: National Monuments have been political footballs since the Antiquities Act came to be in 1906. But so far court cases haven’t changed the president’s authority to shrink or grow them.

rows.title: Denver’s Omnitrax buys San Luis & Rio Grande Railroad, driving hope for economic spark in Colorado’s San Luis Valley
rows.standfirst: The transportation and railroad company Omnitrax acquired the historic 155-mile San Luis & Rio Grande Railroad in a bankruptcy auction with plans for commodity, passenger traffic

rows.title: Colorado’s Ute Mountain Utes get closer to gigabit internet after $22.7 million federal award
rows.standfirst: The federal funds are aimed at connecting unserved tribal communities in Colorado and Utah to broadband

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver inflation slows to 7.7%, which is still historically high
rows.standfirst: Coloradans spent an average of $850 more last month due to inflation, according to one estimate. Plus: CSU researchers say housing prices need to drop 32% for affordability, Starbucks closes unionized store, more!

rows.title: Housing Lottery: Inside a manufactured neighborhood fighting Colorado’s high country housing crisis
rows.standfirst: At Norwood’s Pinion Park, a model to make homes affordable for paycheck-to-paycheck residents is put to the test

rows.title: Xcel Energy will hike its gas rate for a third time this year in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Xcel Energy was OK’d to increase natural gas bills for the third time this year. Consumer advocates say it could have been worse.

rows.title: Colorado housing prices would have to drop 32% to match the “affordability” of 2015
rows.standfirst: The median sales price for a house in 2015 was $285,000.

rows.title: What’s Working: What Colorado’s flat 3.4% unemployment rate means
rows.standfirst: Plus: A $1.6 million contract to revamp the state’s job board, how Boulder’s PopSockets is improving working conditions at factories and more.

rows.title: The wind turbines on his Colorado farm are 20 years old. Who’s going to take them down?
rows.standfirst: The wind industry on the Eastern Plains is running into the same concerns that once plagued the fossil fuel industry.

rows.title: Denverites worried crime would accompany safe outdoor spaces. Data shows the opposite happened.
rows.standfirst: Police said they had no data showing an increase in crimes, and Safe Outdoor Space managers said there have been no residents charged with a crime while living onsite

rows.title: Heidi Ganahl says Colorado’s inflation rate is 16% and the highest in the U.S. Both claims require many asterisks.
rows.standfirst: Ganahl cited a Republican-led analysis to reach that 16% figure. Bureau of Labor Statistics puts inflation at 7.7%. Here’s where the discrepancy comes from.

rows.title: Voters across Colorado’s high country will weigh in on new taxes on short-term rentals, affordable housing proposals
rows.standfirst: As many as 14 Colorado municipalities and counties will ask voters next month to increase or repurpose taxes on short-term rental properties — offered on sites by Airbnb and Vrbo — to help fund affordable housing

rows.title: Colorado is losing another birth center as midwifery struggles to stay profitable despite rising popularity
rows.standfirst: The closure of Thornton’s Seasons Birth Center leaves the state with just six birth centers, which are reimbursed at lower rates by insurance companies

rows.title: Colorado Tourism Office distributing record-setting $1.8M in grants to Front Range, Eastern Plains
rows.standfirst: The federal stimulus and recovery funding will go toward five urban visitors bureaus and two rural communities to help regain tourist traffic lost in the pandemic

rows.title: ESPN sells X Games to MSP Sports Capital, which calls Aspen “a really important cornerstone” of the franchise
rows.standfirst: Aspen Skiing Co. has hosted the Winter X Games since 2002 and has a contract to host the games through 2024.

rows.title: Even with Congress on its side, Crested Butte still can’t stamp out its Amazon-induced postal problems
rows.standfirst: Ongoing U.S. Postal Service issues in the mountain community have Crested Butte residents, town officials at wits’ end

rows.title: Financial help for renters during COVID slashed Colorado evictions by nearly 60%, new study finds
rows.standfirst: The analysis by two nonprofits analyzed 150,000 eviction filings and found stark disparities for those without legal representation

rows.title: New outdoor trade show to be open to the public as Colorado aims to be “the best state for all things outdoor recreation”
rows.standfirst: The Big Gear Show will combine with the (e)revolution e-bike trade show in June 2023 for the outdoor industry’s first-ever business-to-business-to-consumer event

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado is expected to follow the U.S. economy’s slight 3rd quarter growth
rows.standfirst: Despite inflation, job and income growth provided a needed nudge. Plus: The politics of inflation, the state’s VC arm adds its first Black founder-led fund, and more.
